chapter_title: Introduction to Web Design and HTML

topics.topic_name: Web Architecture, URL, DNS and IP Addressing

questions.question: Who invented the World Wide Web (WWW) and created the original HTML markup language in 1989-1990?
questions.explanation: Sir Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web and developed HTML, HTTP, and the first web browser while working at CERN in Switzerland.

questions.question: What is the primary role of the Domain Name System (DNS) on the internet?

options.label: A
options.text: To translate human-friendly domain names into numerical IP addresses

options.label: B
options.text: To compress image files before transmission

options.label: D
options.text: To clean up temporary browser cookies

questions.correct_answer_text: To translate human-friendly domain names into numerical IP addresses
questions.explanation: DNS acts as the internet's phonebook, translating human-readable web addresses (like www.google.com) into numerical IP addresses (like 142.250.190.46) used by routers.

questions.question: How many total bits make up a standard IPv4 internet address?
questions.explanation: An IPv4 address consists of 32 bits divided into 4 octets (bytes) separated by dots, such as 192.168.1.1.

questions.question: How many total bits make up a modern IPv6 address?
questions.explanation: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits in length, represented as 8 hexadecimal groups separated by colons, providing an exponentially vast address space.

questions.question: In the URL 'https://www.example.com/about.html', what does 'https' specify?

options.label: A
options.text: The communication protocol used for secure transfer

options.label: B
options.text: The physical server hard drive label

options.label: D
options.text: The directory path on the local client machine

questions.correct_answer_text: The communication protocol used for secure transfer
questions.explanation: In a URL, the prefix before '://' defines the application protocol (Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure in this case).

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary characteristic of a Static Website?

options.label: A
options.text: Webpages display fixed content to all visitors unless manually updated by the webmaster

options.label: B
options.text: Webpages require a real-time relational SQL database to display any text

options.label: C
options.text: Content changes automatically every minute based on user behavior

options.label: D
options.text: Visitors can directly customize and save database user profiles

questions.correct_answer_text: Webpages display fixed content to all visitors unless manually updated by the webmaster
questions.explanation: A static website serves pre-written HTML/CSS pages directly from the server; the content does not change dynamically unless the underlying source code is manually edited.

questions.question: Which technology is essential for creating an interactive, database-driven Dynamic Website?

options.label: A
options.text: Server-side scripting (e.g. PHP, Python, Node.js) and a Database

options.label: B
options.text: HTML and Notepad text editor only

questions.correct_answer_text: Server-side scripting (e.g. PHP, Python, Node.js) and a Database
questions.explanation: Dynamic websites generate personalized page content on the fly using server-side scripting languages that query backend database management systems.

questions.question: Which of the following online platforms is an example of a Dynamic Website?

options.label: A
options.text: An e-commerce shopping site with personalized carts and user logins

options.label: B
options.text: A single-page static HTML digital restaurant menu

options.label: C
options.text: A plain text document saved on a local desktop

options.label: D
options.text: A scanned PDF flyer posted as an image

questions.correct_answer_text: An e-commerce shopping site with personalized carts and user logins
questions.explanation: E-commerce sites dynamically load product availability, cart state, user accounts, and real-time transaction processing.

questions.question: What is an advantage of a Static Website over a Dynamic Website?

options.label: A
options.text: Faster page loading speed and lower server hosting requirements

options.label: C
options.text: Instant user comment submission without reloading

options.label: D
options.text: Real-time stock market data feeds without refreshing

questions.correct_answer_text: Faster page loading speed and lower server hosting requirements
questions.explanation: Because static sites involve no server-side database queries or script processing, they load extremely fast and consume minimal server resources.

questions.question: Why does updating content on a large Static Website with hundreds of pages become cumbersome?

options.label: A
options.text: Common elements like headers and navigation bars must be manually edited in every single HTML file

options.label: B
options.text: HTML pages automatically delete themselves when updated

options.label: C
options.text: Static pages cannot be read by web browsers

options.label: D
options.text: Static HTML files require recompilation into binary files

questions.correct_answer_text: Common elements like headers and navigation bars must be manually edited in every single HTML file
questions.explanation: Without server-side templates or a CMS database, changes to shared layout elements across hundreds of static HTML files require repetitive manual edits in each file.

questions.question: Which website structure organizes pages in a top-down hierarchy branching from the homepage into categories and sub-pages?
questions.explanation: Tree or hierarchical structure is the most popular website design, branching logically from the root homepage into main sections and sub-pages.

questions.question: A step-by-step online examination or book tutorial where users must navigate pages strictly one after another utilizes which structure?
questions.explanation: Linear structure leads the user through a predefined sequential path using 'Next' and 'Previous' links, suitable for training modules and checkout steps.

questions.question: In which website structure does every webpage contain direct hyperlinks connecting to all other webpages in the site?
questions.explanation: In a web-linked (network/mesh) structure, every page is interconnected with hyperlinks, allowing visitors to jump freely between any two pages.

questions.question: What is a website navigation structure called that combines hierarchical categorization with sequential linear sub-sections?
questions.explanation: A hybrid structure strategically integrates two or more design models (e.g. a hierarchical catalog with a linear multi-step checkout workflow).

questions.question: What is the standard default filename recognized by web servers as the root entry homepage of a website?
questions.explanation: Web servers (Apache, Nginx, IIS) are configured by default to load 'index.html' or 'index.htm' as the primary directory landing page.

questions.question: What does the acronym HTML stand for?
questions.explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language, the standard authoring language used to create documents for display in web browsers.

questions.question: Which tag defines the title displayed on the web browser tab and must be placed inside <head>?
questions.explanation: The `<title>` tag sits inside `<head>` and specifies the document title shown on the browser window or tab title bar.

questions.question: All visible content of a webpage (paragraphs, images, tables, links) must be placed inside which tag?
questions.explanation: The `<body>` element encloses all renderable content visible to website visitors inside the browser viewport.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an 'Empty Tag' (Void Tag) that does NOT have a closing tag in HTML?
questions.explanation:
Empty tags do not enclose content and have no closing tag; common examples are `
`, ``, `
`, and ``.

questions.question: What is the very first line of a modern HTML5 document that informs the browser about the HTML version?
questions.explanation: `<!DOCTYPE html>` is the standard document type declaration (DTD) that instructs modern browsers to render the document in full HTML5 standards mode.

questions.question: Which HTML heading tag renders the largest and most prominent heading?
questions.explanation: HTML defines six heading levels from `<h1>` to `<h6>`, where `<h1>` represents the highest importance and largest font size.

questions.question: Which tag is used to insert a line break without beginning a new paragraph?
questions.explanation:
The `
` tag produces a single line break in text flow without adding the vertical margin space characteristic of `

` paragraphs.

questions.question: To display the chemical formula H2O with '2' as a subscript, which HTML code is correct?
questions.explanation: The `<sub>` tag defines subscript text that appears half a character below the normal baseline, proper for chemical formulas like H2O.

questions.question: To display the algebraic expression x^2 with '2' as a superscript, which HTML code is correct?
questions.explanation: The `<sup>` tag defines superscript text that appears half a character above the normal baseline, used for powers and mathematical exponents.

questions.question: Which HTML tag inserts a horizontal thematic divider line across the webpage?
questions.explanation: The `<hr>` (horizontal rule) tag creates a visual horizontal divider line separating content topics on a webpage.

questions.question: Which HTML tag is used to create a clickable hyperlink?
questions.explanation: The anchor tag `<a>` creates hyperlinks that direct users to another document, webpage, or specific section when clicked.

questions.question: Which attribute of the anchor tag specified the destination URL of the hyperlink?
questions.explanation: The `href` (Hypertext Reference) attribute contains the target URL address to which the hyperlink points.

questions.question: Which target attribute value causes a hyperlink to open the destination page in a NEW browser tab?
questions.explanation: Setting `target="_blank"` instructs the web browser to open the linked document in a new tab or window.

questions.question: What is the difference between an Absolute URL and a Relative URL?

options.label: A
options.text: An absolute URL includes the full protocol and domain name, while a relative URL points to a file path within the same website

options.label: B
options.text: An absolute URL works only on localhost servers

options.label: C
options.text: A relative URL requires a credit card to access

options.label: D
options.text: An absolute URL cannot be used inside anchor tags

questions.correct_answer_text: An absolute URL includes the full protocol and domain name, while a relative URL points to a file path within the same website
questions.explanation: Absolute URLs specify the complete address including protocol and domain (e.g., https://example.com/page.html), while relative URLs relate to the current directory (e.g., page.html).

questions.question: How is a clickable email link created in HTML that opens the user's default email client?
questions.explanation: Using the `mailto:` scheme within `href` instructs the browser to open the user's email program addressed to the specified email recipient.

questions.question: Which tag is used to embed an image into an HTML webpage?
questions.explanation: The `` tag is the standard empty HTML element used to embed graphics and images into an HTML document.

questions.question: Which attribute specifies the file path or web URL of the image in an tag?
questions.explanation: The `src` (source) attribute provides the relative or absolute URL of the image file to be displayed.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'alt' attribute in an element?

options.label: A
options.text: To provide alternative descriptive text if the image fails to load or for screen readers

options.label: B
options.text: To change the brightness and contrast of the image

options.label: C
options.text: To crop the image into a circle

options.label: D
options.text: To convert the image to black and white

questions.correct_answer_text: To provide alternative descriptive text if the image fails to load or for screen readers
questions.explanation: The `alt` (alternative text) attribute displays fallback text if the graphic is missing and assists visually impaired users using screen readers.

questions.question: Which attributes are used to explicitly define the dimensions of an image in pixels?
questions.explanation: The `width` and `height` attributes set the display dimensions of the image in pixels or percentages.

questions.question: Which native HTML5 element allows video playback directly on a webpage without third-party plugins?
questions.explanation: HTML5 introduced the standard `<video>` tag to embed video streams natively into webpages using codecs like H.264/MP4 and WebM.

questions.question: Which tag creates an Ordered (numbered) list in HTML?
questions.explanation: The `<ol>` tag defines an ordered list where each item is marked with numbers, letters, or Roman numerals.

questions.question: Which tag defines an individual item within both ordered (<ol>) and unordered (<ul>) lists?
questions.explanation: The `<li>` (list item) tag wraps each individual entry inside `<ol>` or `<ul>` containers.

questions.question: Which tag creates an Unordered (bulleted) list in HTML?
questions.explanation: The `<ul>` tag creates an unordered list where list items are marked with bullet icons rather than numbers.

questions.question: What will the list items look like if `<ol type="A">` is specified?

options.label: A
options.text: Items labeled with uppercase letters (A, B, C...)

options.label: B
options.text: Items labeled with lowercase Roman numerals (i, ii, iii...)

options.label: C
options.text: Items marked with square bullet dots

questions.correct_answer_text: Items labeled with uppercase letters (A, B, C...)
questions.explanation: The `type="A"` attribute on an `<ol>` tag designates uppercase Latin alphabets as sequential list item markers.

questions.question: Which tag combination defines a Description List containing terms and their explanatory descriptions?
questions.explanation: A description list uses `<dl>` (description list), `<dt>` (description term), and `<dd>` (description definition).

questions.question: Which tag defines an individual row within an HTML table?
questions.explanation: The `<tr>` (table row) tag encloses a horizontal row of cells within an HTML `<table>`.

questions.question: How do standard table header cells (<th>) display content by default compared to data cells (<td>)?
questions.explanation: Text placed inside a `<th>` tag is rendered in bold typeface and centered horizontally by default in web browsers.

questions.question: Which HTML table attribute is used to merge two or more adjacent COLUMNS horizontally into a single cell?
questions.explanation: The `colspan` attribute specifies the number of horizontal columns that a table cell should span.

questions.question: Which HTML table attribute merges two or more vertical ROWS into a single cell?
questions.explanation: The `rowspan` attribute specifies the number of vertical rows a table cell extends across.

questions.question: Which tag defines an accessible title or caption placed directly above or below an HTML table?
questions.explanation: The `<caption>` tag, placed immediately after opening the `<table>` tag, provides an official title for the table.

questions.question: Which input type creates a masked single-line input field where entered characters are hidden by asterisks or dots?
questions.explanation: `<input type="password">` conceals characters typed by the user using bullet dots or asterisks to protect sensitive credentials.

questions.question: Which input control allows a user to select only ONE option from a group of mutually exclusive choices?
questions.explanation: Radio buttons sharing the same `name` attribute permit only a single selection at any time, unlike checkboxes which allow multiple selections.

questions.question: What is the crucial operational difference between HTTP GET and POST form submission methods?

options.label: A
options.text: GET appends submitted form data visibly to the URL address bar, while POST transmits data securely inside the HTTP message body

options.label: B
options.text: GET can only be used with images

options.label: C
options.text: POST deletes the website database upon submission

options.label: D
options.text: GET does not require an internet connection

questions.correct_answer_text: GET appends submitted form data visibly to the URL address bar, while POST transmits data securely inside the HTTP message body
questions.explanation: GET attaches form fields to the query string in the browser URL (making it unsuitable for passwords), whereas POST encapsulates data in the HTTP request payload.

questions.question: Which tag element creates a multi-line plain text input area for messages or comments in an HTML form?
questions.explanation: The `<textarea>` element provides a resizable, multi-line text input field suited for user feedback, articles, or comments.

questions.question: Which protocol is standardly used by web developers to transfer and upload local website files to a remote web hosting server?
questions.explanation: FTP (or secure SFTP) is the standard network protocol used to upload, download, and manage files between a local computer and a remote web server.
